fr:mainmatter.fr:p: CompPoly is a formally verified Lean library for computable polynomial operations over rings and finite fields. I maintain it as part of Protocol Snarkification at the Ethereum Foundation, where it is meant to serve as the computable core underneath ArkLib.

The point of CompPoly is not just to have polynomials in Lean, but to have representations that you can actually run. Mathlib's polynomial types are excellent for abstract algebra, but they are not designed as an executable engine for zero-knowledge verification work. CompPoly provides computable univariate, multivariate, multilinear, and bivariate polynomials, with proved equivalences back to the Mathlib counterparts where that bridge matters. I have written more about why computable specifications matter in this setting.

In broad strokes, the library covers:
Univariate (CPolynomial): coefficient-sequence polynomials with evaluation, interpolation (including Lagrange), and a ring equivalence to Mathlib Polynomial.
Multivariate (CMvPolynomial): sparse monomial maps with a full core API and equivalence to Mathlib MvPolynomial.
Multilinear (CMlPolynomial / CMlPolynomialEval): coefficient and Boolean-hypercube evaluation forms.
Bivariate (CBivariate): nested univariate polynomials with dedicated operations, used heavily in the coding-theory stack.
Fields: concrete finite-field instances (BabyBear, KoalaBear, Goldilocks, and others), Montgomery arithmetic, computable field extensions, and binary-field / additive-NTT infrastructure.
Coding theory: Reed-Solomon encoding, Gao unique decoding, and Guruswami-Sudan list decoding, with proved correctness.

Phase 1 of the roadmap—the theoretical foundation—is essentially complete: core algebraic structure, API coverage, and Mathlib bridges are in place. The current focus is Phase 2, performance and efficiency: faster field arithmetic, FFT/NTT-based multiplication, and better evaluation/interpolation pathways, without giving up proof-first correctness. See the roadmap for the live status.

My own role has shifted over Q1 2026 from doing a large share of the Phase 1 formalization toward coordinating a much larger contributor base for Phase 2—style, CI, contribution standards, and making sure the pieces fit together. I also gave a talk on CompPoly at ZKProofs 8.
